# Commonness and coverage review

Reviewed October 16, 2026. This is a catalog coverage decision, not a recommendation that a student should prefer the most common job.

Every one of the 857 directory-only O*NET titles received an explicit decision and a named field. The baseline was 67 reviewed careers and 923 official O*NET directory titles. Sixty-six reviewed careers are exact directory matches; tattooing is an editorial role outside that directory. The 50 proposed additions are distinct existing directory titles. The remaining 807 stay nested under fields, with official links.

## How the 50 were chosen

We used actual employment headcounts, field gaps, and distinct preparation routes. We did not use salary, fame, prestige, social-media popularity, or projected percentage growth as a substitute for how common the work is. The selection is an editorial coverage set, not the mathematical largest 50 occupations. It deliberately includes retail, office support, food service, cleaning, warehouses, care work, and ordinary skilled work alongside college and graduate professions.

The previous catalog already covers many science, engineering, health, and creative careers. Adding more specialties in those fields would leave much larger gaps in other everyday work. Chemical and aerospace engineering, performing arts, and medical specialties remain grouped under the relevant fields; they are not excluded as student possibilities.

Management destinations are included where common, but their related-experience requirements remain visible. A first qualified management job is not assumed to be a first job after school. Actors and musicians are deferred from salary-driven additions because official pay is hourly and engagements are irregular; converting their hourly rates into 2,080-hour annual salaries would be misleading.

## Employment evidence and limits

- **National:** [BLS 2025 National Employment Matrix, Table 1.2](https://www.bls.gov/emp/tables/occupational-projections-and-characteristics.htm), released August 27, 2026. Employment includes self-employed workers and is published in thousands, rounded to one decimal. All 831 line-item occupation groups were parsed. The web archive covers every source line and contains no conflicting overlapping table cells.
- **Austin/Travis area:** [TWC 2024–2034 projections](https://texaswages.com/Projections), [Capital Area data](https://texaswages.com/api/Proj/14). We use **2024 base employment**, not 2034 forecasts or job openings. This is workforce area 14, Austin/Travis County, **not the five-county Austin metropolitan area**. Not every detailed occupation has an unsuppressed local row.
- **Current Austin metro check:** [BLS May 2025 Austin release](https://www.bls.gov/regions/southwest/news-release/OccupationalEmploymentandWages_Austin.htm), August 13, 2026. Office support, management, and food service are major local employment groups. Its computing table reports 9,680 user-support specialists, 800 web developers, and 1,080 web/interface designers. These counts have a different geography and employment scope from the TWC baseline and are stored separately.

O*NET specialty titles often share a BLS parent occupation. We attach the parent's source code and scope to each title, but we do not turn the shared number into an independently measured specialty count. Totals use distinct BLS line-item codes only; never sum the 857 title-level references. A missing local row means unavailable, not zero workers.

The single title without a separate national line-item count in the reviewed matrix is Legislators. Its official O*NET page uses the much broader Top Executives group. We retain that as labeled context and exclude it from role ranking and count totals; inventing a legislator count would be inappropriate.

## Financial evidence

All 50 proposed additions have May 2025 Austin employee wage rows, with 25th percentile, median, and 75th percentile values, plus TWC's official entry proxy. No geographic fallback is needed for this set. TWC entry means the mean of the lowest-paid third; it is not observed pay at zero years of experience. Later experience stages require explicit illustrative-scenario labeling.

Two mappings use combined BLS categories: personal care aides use home health/personal care aide pay; mental-health counselors use combined substance-abuse, behavioral-disorder, and mental-health counselor pay. These wider scopes are recorded. Employee wages exclude self-employment and owner profit; tips, commissions, working hours, business costs, and unpaid gaps matter for restaurant service, photography, personal care, and sales.

## Verification

The scripts verify 857 unique decisions, exactly 50 additions, 807 grouped titles, source-line coverage, 831 national line-item employment groups, no conflicting source cells, and complete wage/entry-proxy coverage for the new 50. These checks establish data handling and coverage; they do not validate aptitude, individual career suitability, future earnings, or guaranteed job availability.
